outcome: Forecast, place and scale multiplayer capacity to hold latency and availability targets at a verified lower cost per player-session
overview: Launch spikes, seasonal events and regional demand leave platform teams choosing between overprovisioned fleets that burn cash and thin capacity that produces queue failures and unplayable latency. This solution forecasts session demand by region and hour, places and scales game-server fleets against agreed latency and availability objectives, and reports verified cost per player-session rather than aggregate cloud spend. Guardrails matter as much as savings: quotas, canaries, multi-zone placement, human approval for structural changes and rehearsed rollback. An 8–12-week proof of value on one title or region targets a 10–20% reduction in cost per session while service objectives hold through injected failure.

benefits.text: Reduce cost per player-session by 10–20% while latency and availability objectives hold
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Verified against the customer’s own cloud billing and session counts; savings depend on current utilisation and how much headroom the existing design already carries

benefits.text: Meet launch and seasonal capacity targets without emergency overprovisioning
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Forecast accuracy depends on comparable historical launches; a first title in a new market has no demand history to learn from

benefits.text: Hold service objectives through zone and provider failure with rehearsed, auditable recovery
benefits.source: Reference architecture resilience design, Redington Gaming catalogue
benefits.limits: Demonstrated through injected failure and chaos testing in the proof of value; provider-wide or region-wide outages remain disruptive

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA, Bahrain) for Gulf player latency; session telemetry and billing data remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.why: Forecasting and cost-per-session reporting both need historical demand by region and hour; without it there is no baseline and no verifiable saving

notFor.situation: No deployment automation for game-server fleets
notFor.why: Automated scaling and placement require repeatable, automated deployment; manual fleet changes cannot be canaried or rolled back safely

notFor.situation: No agreed latency and availability service objectives
notFor.why: Cost optimisation without objectives is just cost cutting; there is nothing to protect the player experience against

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns service objectives, scaling policy approval and production change control · Duration: 8–12-week proof of value; further 16–28 weeks to portfolio scale
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, platform and Kubernetes engineer, network specialist, FinOps analyst; customer platform or SRE owner, network engineer, security reviewer, finance analyst · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and cost-per-session and SLO baseline agreement
2) Telemetry, billing and fleet integration
3) Demand forecasting and capacity-policy build
4) Quota, canary and chaos-test configuration
5) Proof of value on one title or region with repeated launch simulations
6) Stabilisation and handover
deliverables: Representative load test passed at forecast peak concurrency
Service objectives held throughout scaling and placement changes
Autoscaling behaviour verified in both directions, including the warm-capacity floor
Failure and recovery drills passed for zone loss and provider component failure
Cost guardrails and quotas verified; security review and operations user-acceptance testing complete
